agenda.title: One counter staff short for the opening rush

briefing.text: Siti texted at quarter to seven, her kid's in hospital, so we're one short at the counter for the rush at 8.

knownBy.why: you got the text this morning
you've been setting up the counter

briefing.text: We sent free-kopi flyers to every office in the building, about 200 of them.

knownBy.why: you sent the flyers out
you know the crowd it brings

agenda.decision: how do we cover the counter from 8 to 10 one person short?
directions: Ask Auntie Mary to come in. Rest-day work is double pay and she can say no. If asked, she answers once, in character: she may agree, refuse, or agree with a condition such as only from 9. Decide her answer from how the guest asks.
An agency temp needs notice and a till login from Arjun, which takes about 15 minutes before opening; the temp does not know the menu.
A manager covers the counter. Whoever it is drops their own opening-day job.
Cut the counter menu to drinks and toast only, or push ordering to the kiosk.
Scale back the free-kopi offer.
background: The free-kopi crowd is expected from 8 to 9, and the counter has two staff before anyone is added.

offScreen.name: Auntie Mary
offScreen.howTheyAnswer: Auntie Mary answers once, in character. She may agree, refuse, or agree with a condition such as starting at 9. A warm, fair ask is more likely to get a yes; decide her answer from how the guest asks.

seatFacts.producer: I signed off on today's roster. Auntie Mary is on her rest day, so calling her in means double pay, and she's free to say no.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: Setting up a till login for someone new takes me about 15 minutes before opening.
seatFacts.game_designer: Toast sets are what slow the counter down; drinks ordered on the kiosk barely touch the counter.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: Our free-kopi flyers went to every office in the building, about 200 of them.

tradeOffs.question: Who is actually going to stand on that counter with them from 8?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: A temp needs a till login, that's fifteen minutes of mine. And they won't know the menu.
tradeOffs.question: What do you want me to set up for a temp before eight?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Then whoever it is drops their own job this morning.
tradeOffs.question: Which job do we drop if a manager takes the counter?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Then there are no breakfast sets on opening day.
tradeOffs.question: What do we tell people who came for a breakfast set?

agenda.title: Old regulars and the new kopi prices

briefing.text: Kopi's gone from $1.30 to $2.40, and some of the old uncles saw that yesterday and just walked out.

knownBy.why: you were there when the regulars walked out
you saw them leave

briefing.text: One of their nephews posted on Facebook that we've forgotten our roots, and it has a few hundred shares already.

knownBy.why: you saw the Facebook post
the post is about our menu

agenda.decision: what do we do for the old regulars without losing money on every cup?
directions: An old-price hour for kopi before the rush: it loses money per cup and keeps the counter busy.

A regulars' card or a regulars' price on the till. Arjun can add a price button in about 10 minutes, but may not have time to test it before opening. Someone must decide who counts as a regular. If the guest proposes a list of names, a colleague may offer to ask Uncle Lim, who answers once after that ask: he may offer to vouch for them, or say he will not be the one turning people away.
A seniors' discount checked against a seniors' card: simple to check, but not every regular is a senior, and office workers' parents qualify too.
Hold the price and explain it: a note at the counter, a reply on Facebook, a free first kopi for regulars this week.
background: This flagship is the refurbished old Nanyang shop; many morning regulars have come here for years, and photos of the old regulars hang on the wall.
Uncle Lim has run the kopi bar since the old shop.

offScreen.name: Uncle Lim
offScreen.howTheyAnswer: Uncle Lim answers once, in character. He may offer to vouch for the regulars, or say he will not be the one turning people away. Decide his answer from how the guest asks.

seatFacts.producer: Kopi costs us about $1.60 a cup to serve here. Going back to the old $1.30 loses money on every cup.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: I can add a regulars' price button on the till in about 10 minutes, but we need a clear rule on who gets it.
seatFacts.game_designer: Kopi was $1.30 at the old shop and it's $2.40 on the new menu, right under the photos of the old regulars on our wall.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: The nephew's Facebook post has been shared a few hundred times since last night. The food blogger reads those local groups.

openingViews.angle: the old shop's regulars and the photos on the wall

tradeOffs.tradeOff: A cup costs us about $1.60 to make here. At $1.30, we lose money on every one.
tradeOffs.question: How do we do right by the uncles without selling kopi at a loss?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: I can add the button in ten minutes. But who decides who's a regular? The cashier?
tradeOffs.question: How do we decide who gets the regulars' price at the till?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Not all our regulars are seniors. And half the office workers' parents would qualify.
tradeOffs.question: How do we look after the old regulars who aren't seniors?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: We put the uncles' photos on the wall, then priced them out. A note at the counter won't fix that.
tradeOffs.question: How do we look after the old regulars without gutting the new menu?

agenda.title: Laptop campers and the breakfast seat crunch

briefing.text: Yesterday the laptop crowd took about half our seats, two hours each, on one kopi.

knownBy.why: you were on the floor at the trial
your crew was on the floor

briefing.text: Breakfast customers walked out holding their trays, and one of my floor staff got shouted at for asking someone to move.

knownBy.why: it was your crew who got shouted at
you saw the breakfast crowd leave

agenda.decision: how do we keep seats turning for the breakfast crowd without putting floor staff in a fight?
directions: Booth power off and Wi-Fi limited from 8 to 10: the socket timer and Wi-Fi codes take about 10 minutes to change, with little time to test before opening. Many of the laptop users work upstairs.
A laptop zone on the 10 window-bar stools with power, and breakfast-table signs on the booths.
A minimum spend per hour for laptop seats, shown on a time-stamped receipt, so staff have to check.
A deal for the offices upstairs, which is Daniel's angle.
background: Many laptop users work in the offices upstairs.

seatFacts.producer: Losing those tables cost us about $420 in breakfast sales yesterday, and our floor crew shouldn't be getting yelled at over seats.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: The booth sockets are all on one timer switch, and I can set the Wi-Fi to print a 45-minute code on each receipt in about 10 minutes.
seatFacts.game_designer: Most morning customers come in alone with a hot tray, and we have ten window-bar stools in the storeroom we can put out.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: Over half the laptop crowd wore lanyards from the offices upstairs, and a couple of those offices have asked about bulk orders.

links.with: One counter staff short for the opening rush
links.effect: With nobody spare to walk the floor, any seat rule has to work on its own.
How we treat the laptop crowd from upstairs affects whether their offices take up a direct order code.

openingViews.angle: can change the booth plugs and Wi-Fi before eight, but needs to know the goal first
the laptop crowd works upstairs and their offices might order in bulk

tradeOffs.tradeOff: I can, the plugs are on one timer. But it's ten minutes, and I can't test it before 8.
tradeOffs.question: What do you want me to change before eight, if anything?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: The window bar's only got ten stools. That won't hold half the shop.
tradeOffs.question: What do we do when the window bar fills up?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Then my floor staff are checking receipts. That's exactly the fight we had yesterday.
tradeOffs.question: How do we enforce a minimum spend without a fight at the counter?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: A deal doesn't free up a seat by 8.
tradeOffs.question: How does a deal upstairs free a seat down here by eight?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Those are the offices I've spent weeks winning over. Push their people out and the bulk orders go with them.
tradeOffs.question: How do we free up the breakfast booths without chasing away the office crowd upstairs?

agenda.title: Food safety complaint before the 9 AM inspection
agenda.spoken: food safety and the 9 o'clock routine check

briefing.text: The fridge was off three hours last night, the chef threw out all the eggs and kaya, and there's no Set A till the 10 o'clock delivery, which is our best seller.

knownBy.why: you went through the fridge log
the head chef told you when you checked the eggs and kaya this morning

briefing.text: A customer who ate here yesterday, before the fridge went off, emailed to say she got sick and had to see a doctor.

knownBy.why: her email came to you
it came across your desk

agenda.decision: do we open at 8, and what do we tell the customer and the inspector?
directions: Open at 8 without Set A until the 10 o'clock delivery.
Open at 10 after the inspection, with a big loss of morning sales and the free-kopi crowd.
Open with an honest note at the counter.
For the customer: apology and refund, and cover her clinic bill, which is $85, or offer something more.
A socket cover and a fridge temperature alert, which take about 10 minutes to set up before opening.
background: The night cleaner unplugged the fridge to use the socket.
The head chef found it at 6:10, threw out everything in it and signed a disposal log.
The customer is recovering at home. Nobody is being fired; the cleaner gets retraining and the socket gets a cover.
The eggs and kaya are gone until the 10 o'clock delivery.
If Set A is off until 10, it comes off the kiosk and the till too, which costs Arjun minutes.
The food agency officer's visit at 9 is a routine opening-day check booked weeks ago; it is not a response to the complaint.
The customer ate Set A at yesterday's trial, before the fridge was unplugged overnight, so the fridge is probably not the cause.

seatFacts.producer: I signed the hygiene sign-off for HQ. The chef signed the disposal log, and the fridge log shows the three-hour gap last night. The officer will ask for both. Our insurer allows a goodwill payment without admitting fault.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: The fridge has no alarm. I was asked for a POS temperature alert last month; it takes about ten minutes. I can also remove Set A from the till and kiosk.
seatFacts.game_designer: I designed Set A. It's our biggest breakfast seller, and it needs eggs and kaya. We have no fresh stock until the 10 o'clock delivery.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: Her email is polite, but she says she'll post a review tonight. The food blogger is booked for later this morning.

links.with: Old regulars and the new kopi prices
links.effect: With the nephew's Facebook post already up, a bad hygiene review tonight would be our second public hit on day one.
With Set A off until 10, we cannot send Set A out on GrabFood or in office platters before 10 either.

openingViews.angle: getting Set A off the till and kiosk before opening
the crowd at the door and the review tonight

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Then I've got to pull Set A off the kiosk and the till. That's time I'm not testing anything else.
tradeOffs.question: What do you want me to pull before opening?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: We'd miss the whole free-kopi crowd. The building turns up to a closed door.
tradeOffs.question: What do we tell the customer and the crowd at the door?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: She's posting a review tonight. A refund on its own might read like we're brushing her off.
tradeOffs.question: What do we say to her beyond an apology?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: The alarm's ten minutes. Fine, but that's ten minutes less for everything else.
tradeOffs.question: What do you want me to fix before the inspector arrives?

agenda.title: Delivery app commission squeeze

briefing.text: GrabFood's promo rate on their cut ended today for all our shops, so every breakfast set we deliver from here now loses us 50 cents.

knownBy.why: you've run the numbers
you watch the app orders

briefing.text: And most of those orders come from the offices in this building.

knownBy.why: you've been watching the app orders
you saw the app traffic

agenda.decision: how do we stop losing 50 cents on every delivered set without losing the office orders?
directions: Raise the app price. GrabFood hides shops that charge more on the app than at the counter.
Office Platters for five or more, limited by the large trays.
A direct pickup code for offices. Someone has to come down; a pickup shelf sits by the side door.
Pause single sets on the app from 8 to 10. Daniel's launch deal gives a featured banner only while the full menu is live.
Any app menu change takes 15 minutes to go live and leaves less time for Arjun to test other changes before opening.
background: GrabFood's promo rate on its cut for all our shops ended today.
Commission is 32%: $10.00 less 32% leaves $6.80, and a delivered set costs $7.30 to make and pack, so the loss is $0.50 per set.
A five-set Office Platter at $50 costs $29 with shared packaging, keeps $34 and makes $5 profit.
Direct pickup with 10% off takes $9.00 in, costs $7.00 with no delivery packaging, and makes $2 profit.

seatFacts.producer: A single delivered set costs us $7.30 to make and pack, so we lose 50 cents a set, and on a full morning that adds up to about $120. A five-set platter at $50 shares packaging and makes $5.
seatFacts.lead_programmer: GrabFood hides shops that charge more on the app than at the counter, and any app menu change takes me about 15 minutes to push live before 8.
seatFacts.game_designer: Each five-set platter needs one of our large trays, and we only have 30 of those trays in the shop.
seatFacts.marketing_lead: A dozen office managers have asked me for a direct order code, and most office orders are for several sets. We keep the GrabFood launch banner only while the full menu is live.

links.with: Food safety complaint before the 9 AM inspection
links.effect: With Set A off until 10, we cannot send Set A out on GrabFood or in office platters before 10 either.

openingViews.angle: the app orders, the office managers and the launch banner
the numbers: 50 cents lost on a set and the platter that makes $5

tradeOffs.tradeOff: GrabFood hides shops that charge more on the app than at the counter. We'd just disappear.
tradeOffs.question: What happens to our listing if we raise the app price?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Each platter needs a big tray, and we've only got 30.
tradeOffs.question: How many platters can we actually make this morning?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Someone has to come down to pick it up. At 8 in the morning, will they?
tradeOffs.question: How do we make a direct pickup code work at 8 in the morning?

tradeOffs.tradeOff: Pull anything off GrabFood and we lose our launch banner, the free ad at the top of the app.
tradeOffs.question: How do we keep the office orders without losing our GrabFood launch banner?

situation: It's 7 AM on opening day at our refurbished Raffles Place flagship, and doors open at 8. Yesterday's trial day and this morning have left us a few things to sort out first.
background: The shop has booths and tables, a kiosk, a kopi bar and a kitchen. The team has an hour before doors open.
The till, kiosk, power sockets and Wi-Fi all need Arjun for changes. Nothing he changes this morning has been tested yet.
The offices upstairs are customers. The shop has worked with a staffing agency before.
People in the rush, Arjun's time before opening and the menu are shared resources.

glossary.Kopi: coffee brewed the Nanyang way, usually with condensed milk unless you ask otherwise
glossary.Kopi O Kosong: black coffee with no sugar and no milk
glossary.Set A: kaya butter toast with two soft-boiled eggs and a hot kopi or tea
glossary.kiosk: the self-order screen with 24 drinks at the front of the shop
glossary.POS: point-of-sale system (the till, the kiosk and the kitchen tickets)
glossary.kopi bar: the counter where Uncle Lim pulls kopi and knows the regulars by name
